run-ref: 1c7203ea0da5406b4937d80f6013564a

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

run-ref: 1c7203ea0da5406b4937d80f6013564a

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers see "processing" then "rejected" since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact first-rejection timestamp per that component's journal.

- Tool calls made and results:
  - queue_stats for hour 11:00 on all 6 queues: q.pike-scan, q.nimbus-split, q.amber-ocr, q.cinder-extract, q.ember-index, q.tundra-notify.
  - Only q.amber-ocr showed rejections: row 11:40 rejected=39, row 11:50 rejected=45; hour totals: enqueued 1615, done 1507, rejected 84, requeued 221, longest wait 2711s (at 11:50). All other queues showed rejected=0 for every 10-min row and the hour total (pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify) — ruled out as the rejecting component. ember-index and pike-scan/nimbus-split had high depth/wait but zero rejections, so they are backed up/congested but not rejecting.
  - Conclusion: q.amber-ocr (component "amber-ocr") is the rejecting component. Rejections first appear in the 11:30–11:40 stats window (first nonzero in 11:40 row), so journal for amber-ocr hour 11:00 was pulled to find exact first event.

- Journal reads (component=amber-ocr, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
  - Page 1 (seq 236017–236074, times 11:00:00–11:03:40): only received/leased/progress/completed events, no rejections or retries yet.
  - Page 8 (seq 236423–236480, times 11:27:00–11:31:36): still no rejections/retries, normal flow.
  - Page 10 (seq 236539–236596, times 11:35:28–11:39:55): first "retry" events appear ("lease lost before completion; returned to queue", attempts 1–2 of 5), but no "job-rejected" events yet.
  - Page 11 (seq 236597–236654, times 11:40:00–11:43:26): retries continue (attempts escalate up to attempt 4 of 5 for J-ZJAMHRDQ/tn-2305). First "job-rejected" event found at:
    - seq 236622 | time 11:41:49.157 | job J-ZJAMHRDQ | tenant tn-2305 | event job-rejected | detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified"
    - Subsequent job-rejected events follow shortly after (236624 at 11:41:51.712, 236625 at 11:41:52.744, etc.), confirming 11:41:49.157 is the first.

- Hypothesis confirmed: amber-ocr is the rejecting pipeline component; rejections are caused by jobs losing their worker lease repeatedly (retry events) and being rejected after exhausting 5 delivery attempts.
- Hypotheses ruled out: pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify — none show any rejected jobs in queue_stats for the 11:00 hour.
- No further pages needed; first_rejection_time confirmed as the earliest "job-rejected" event in the journal (seq 236622, page 11).

- Next step: finalize answer with verbatim values.

```json
{"rejecting_component": "amber-ocr", "first_rejection_time": "11:41:49.157"}
```
</summary_of_earlier_work>

run-ref: 1c7203ea0da5406b4937d80f6013564a

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers see "processing" then "rejected" since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact first-rejection timestamp per that component's journal.

- Tool calls made and results:
  - queue_stats for hour 11:00 on all 6 queues: q.pike-scan, q.nimbus-split, q.amber-ocr, q.cinder-extract, q.ember-index, q.tundra-notify.
  - Only q.amber-ocr showed rejections: row 11:40 rejected=39, row 11:50 rejected=45; hour totals: enqueued 1615, done 1507, rejected 84, requeued 221, longest wait 2711s (at 11:50). All other queues showed rejected=0 for every 10-min row and the hour total (pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify) — ruled out as the rejecting component. ember-index and pike-scan/nimbus-split had high depth/wait but zero rejections, so they are backed up/congested but not rejecting.
  - Conclusion: q.amber-ocr (component "amber-ocr") is the rejecting component. Rejections first appear in the 11:30–11:40 stats window (first nonzero in 11:40 row), so journal for amber-ocr hour 11:00 was pulled to find exact first event.

- Journal reads (component=amber-ocr, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
  - Page 1 (seq 236017–236074, times 11:00:00–11:03:40): only received/leased/progress/completed events, no rejections or retries yet.
  - Page 8 (seq 236423–236480, times 11:27:00–11:31:36): still no rejections/retries, normal flow.
  - Page 10 (seq 236539–236596, times 11:35:28–11:39:55): first "retry" events appear ("lease lost before completion; returned to queue", attempts 1–2 of 5), but no "job-rejected" events yet.
  - Page 11 (seq 236597–236654, times 11:40:00–11:43:26): retries continue (attempts escalate up to attempt 4 of 5 for J-ZJAMHRDQ/tn-2305). First "job-rejected" event found at:
    - seq 236622 | time 11:41:49.157 | job J-ZJAMHRDQ | tenant tn-2305 | event job-rejected | detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified"
    - Subsequent job-rejected events follow shortly after (236624 at 11:41:51.712, 236625 at 11:41:52.744, etc.), confirming 11:41:49.157 is the first.

- Hypothesis confirmed: amber-ocr is the rejecting pipeline component; rejections are caused by jobs losing their worker lease repeatedly (retry events) and being rejected after exhausting 5 delivery attempts.
- Hypotheses ruled out: pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify — none show any rejected jobs in queue_stats for the 11:00 hour.
- No further pages needed; first_rejection_time confirmed as the earliest "job-rejected" event in the journal (seq 236622, page 11).

- Next step: finalize answer with verbatim values.

```json
{"rejecting_component": "amber-ocr", "first_rejection_time": "11:41:49.157"}
```
</summary_of_earlier_work>

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers see "processing" then "rejected" since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact first-rejection timestamp per that component's journal.

- Tool calls made and results:
  - queue_stats for hour 11:00 on all 6 queues: q.pike-scan, q.nimbus-split, q.amber-ocr, q.cinder-extract, q.ember-index, q.tundra-notify.
  - Only q.amber-ocr showed rejections: row 11:40 rejected=39, row 11:50 rejected=45; hour totals: enqueued 1615, done 1507, rejected 84, requeued 221, longest wait 2711s (at 11:50). All other queues showed rejected=0 for every 10-min row and the hour total (pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify) — ruled out as the rejecting component. ember-index and pike-scan/nimbus-split had high depth/wait but zero rejections, so they are backed up/congested but not rejecting.
  - Conclusion: q.amber-ocr (component "amber-ocr") is the rejecting component. Rejections first appear in the 11:30–11:40 stats window (first nonzero in 11:40 row), so journal for amber-ocr hour 11:00 was pulled to find exact first event.

- Journal reads (component=amber-ocr, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
  - Page 1 (seq 236017–236074, times 11:00:00–11:03:40): only received/leased/progress/completed events, no rejections or retries yet.
  - Page 8 (seq 236423–236480, times 11:27:00–11:31:36): still no rejections/retries, normal flow.
  - Page 10 (seq 236539–236596, times 11:35:28–11:39:55): first "retry" events appear ("lease lost before completion; returned to queue", attempts 1–2 of 5), but no "job-rejected" events yet.
  - Page 11 (seq 236597–236654, times 11:40:00–11:43:26): retries continue (attempts escalate up to attempt 4 of 5 for J-ZJAMHRDQ/tn-2305). First "job-rejected" event found at:
    - seq 236622 | time 11:41:49.157 | job J-ZJAMHRDQ | tenant tn-2305 | event job-rejected | detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified"
    - Subsequent job-rejected events follow shortly after (236624 at 11:41:51.712, 236625 at 11:41:52.744, etc.), confirming 11:41:49.157 is the first.

- Hypothesis confirmed: amber-ocr is the rejecting pipeline component; rejections are caused by jobs losing their worker lease repeatedly (retry events) and being rejected after exhausting 5 delivery attempts.
- Hypotheses ruled out: pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify — none show any rejected jobs in queue_stats for the 11:00 hour.
- No further pages needed; first_rejection_time confirmed as the earliest "job-rejected" event in the journal (seq 236622, page 11).

- Next step: finalize answer with verbatim values.

<task>
Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.
</task>

<transcript_to_summarise>
{"id": "sum1", "role": "summary", "body": "- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers see "processing" then "rejected" since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact first-rejection timestamp per that component's journal.

- Tool calls made and results:
  - queue_stats for hour 11:00 on all 6 queues: q.pike-scan, q.nimbus-split, q.amber-ocr, q.cinder-extract, q.ember-index, q.tundra-notify.
  - Only q.amber-ocr showed rejections: row 11:40 rejected=39, row 11:50 rejected=45; hour totals: enqueued 1615, done 1507, rejected 84, requeued 221, longest wait 2711s (at 11:50). All other queues showed rejected=0 for every 10-min row and the hour total (pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify) — ruled out as the rejecting component. ember-index and pike-scan/nimbus-split had high depth/wait but zero rejections, so they are backed up/congested but not rejecting.
  - Conclusion: q.amber-ocr (component "amber-ocr") is the rejecting component. Rejections first appear in the 11:30–11:40 stats window (first nonzero in 11:40 row), so journal for amber-ocr hour 11:00 was pulled to find exact first event.

- Journal reads (component=amber-ocr, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
  - Page 1 (seq 236017–236074, times 11:00:00–11:03:40): only received/leased/progress/completed events, no rejections or retries yet.
  - Page 8 (seq 236423–236480, times 11:27:00–11:31:36): still no rejections/retries, normal flow.
  - Page 10 (seq 236539–236596, times 11:35:28–11:39:55): first "retry" events appear ("lease lost before completion; returned to queue", attempts 1–2 of 5), but no "job-rejected" events yet.
  - Page 11 (seq 236597–236654, times 11:40:00–11:43:26): retries continue (attempts escalate up to attempt 4 of 5 for J-ZJAMHRDQ/tn-2305). First "job-rejected" event found at:
    - seq 236622 | time 11:41:49.157 | job J-ZJAMHRDQ | tenant tn-2305 | event job-rejected | detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified"
    - Subsequent job-rejected events follow shortly after (236624 at 11:41:51.712, 236625 at 11:41:52.744, etc.), confirming 11:41:49.157 is the first.

- Hypothesis confirmed: amber-ocr is the rejecting pipeline component; rejections are caused by jobs losing their worker lease repeatedly (retry events) and being rejected after exhausting 5 delivery attempts.
- Hypotheses ruled out: pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify — none show any rejected jobs in queue_stats for the 11:00 hour.
- No further pages needed; first_rejection_time confirmed as the earliest "job-rejected" event in the journal (seq 236622, page 11).

- Next step: finalize answer with verbatim values.

```json
{"rejecting_component": "amber-ocr", "first_rejection_time": "11:41:49.157"}
```"}

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task progression (prior Q&A, all answered):
  1) Q: which pipeline component rejects jobs & first rejection time (journal)? A: component "amber-ocr", first_rejection_time "11:41:49.157" (job J-ZJAMHRDQ, tenant tn-2305, seq 236622, detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified"). Confirmed via queue_stats (only q.amber-ocr had rejected>0: row 11:40 rejected=39, row 11:50 rejected=45, hour total rejected=84, enqueued 1615, done 1507, requeued 221, longest wait 2711s at 11:50) and journal paging (pages 1,8,9,10,11 of 15 read). Other queues (pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify) had rejected=0 all intervals — ruled out.
  2) Q: which config change (2hrs before 11:41:49) is responsible? A: faulty_change = "CHG-67658" (amber-ocr, 2026-01-20 11:04 UTC, by team-Heron, status=applied, "set worker.lease_seconds: 600 -> 45", note "align worker settings with the new capacity plan"). Checked list_changes for all 7 components (amber-ocr, moss-intake, pike-scan, nimbus-split, cinder-extract, ember-index, tundra-notify); only CHG-67658 plausibly explains lease-loss retries/rejections (other changes were unrelated log-level/log-sampling tweaks or ember-index's commit_interval change at 11:31, which postdates first rejection and is irrelevant).
  3) Q: rejected_jobs count in 11:00-12:00 queue_stats for amber-ocr? A: rejected_jobs = 84 (hour total, confirmed above).
  4) Current Q (in progress): "Quote one line from that component's 11:00-12:00 UTC journal that states the configuration setting behind the problem, with its value." Need one journal line (not queue_stats, not list_changes) literally naming the setting (worker.lease_seconds) and its value within the amber-ocr 11:00 hour journal.

  - Page 11 (seq 236597–236654, 11:40:00–11:43:26): retries continue to attempt 4 of 5; first job-rejected at seq 236622 (11:41:49.157); more job-rejected events follow (236624, 236625, 236634, 236635, 236642, 236643, 236646, 236648, 236651). None of these lines explicitly state "worker.lease_seconds" or its value — they only describe "lease lost before completion" / "rejected after 5 delivery attempts".

- Unresolved: have not yet found a journal line that explicitly states the setting name (worker.lease_seconds) and value (45 or 600->45). Pages not yet checked: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15. Most likely candidate is near 11:04 UTC (when CHG-67658 applied) — i.e., page 3 (seq range immediately after page 2's 236132, continuing past 11:07) — should check page 3 next for a possible "config applied"/"setting changed" style journal entry mentioning worker.lease_seconds explicitly. A: component "amber-ocr", first_rejection_time "11:41:49.157" (job J-ZJAMHRDQ, tenant tn-2305, seq 236622, detail "rejected after 5 delivery attempts; customer notified").   P-4.3 (restore): revert the change that set lease_seconds through the change log, then drain the retry queue
  P-4.4 (verify): watch the next two ten-minute rows of the queue statistics return to normal

Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

Found it on page 13: seq 236733, time 11:48:51.372, job J-TC7FX8W5, tenant tn-4735, event "diagnostic", detail: "processing took 476 s but worker.lease_seconds=45, so the lease expired mid-job and the job was redelivered"

```

parts.content:
playbook: symptom catalogue
  SYM-SCAN-HOLD  uploads are quarantined by the malware scanner and rejected  (section: scan-quarantine)
  SYM-INDEX-LAG  search results lag behind because the index queue is backed up  (section: index-backlog)
  SYM-TENANT-QUOTA  one tenant's jobs are refused because it has reached its quota  (section: tenant-quota)
  SYM-LEASE-SHORT  jobs keep returning to the queue before they finish and are eventually rejected  (section: lease-starvation)
  SYM-HOOK-DROP  customers stop receiving completion webhooks  (section: webhook-delivery-failures)
  SYM-WORKER-MEM  workers die partway through larger documents and the jobs are eventually rejected  (section: worker-memory-exhaustion)
  SYM-PAGE-CAP  documents above a certain length are refused at the split stage and rejected  (section: page-cap-rejections)

playbook: lease-starvation (SYM-LEASE-SHORT)
what you see: jobs keep returning to the queue before they finish and are eventually rejected
procedure:
  P-4.1 (confirm): check the queue statistics and the component's journal for the pattern above
  P-4.2 (contain): pause new uploads for the affected tenants if the backlog keeps growing
  P-4.3 (restore): revert the change that set lease_seconds through the change log, then drain the retry queue
  P-4.4 (verify): watch the next two ten-minute rows of the queue statistics return to normal

- When the request grows past 70% of the budget, the runtime asks a summariser to replace older parts of this conversation with a summary. The most recent messages are kept verbatim up to about 4800 tokens (the newest message is kept even if larger, when it fits); older messages, and recent messages too large for that allowance, are summarised. Summaries are sized to leave room for further work.
